hook.line: At the café, nobody cares who sold the last lunch or who signed the contract. They care that it happened. English says *was sold* and *was signed*; Spanish uses a little word you already know, *se*.

examples.en: It will be signed on Monday.

rule:
When it doesn't matter who did something, Spanish puts *se* before the verb and lets the thing be the subject.

*Se vendió la casa*: the house was sold.
*Se vendieron las casas*: the houses were sold.

The verb agrees with the thing, not with *se*: one thing, one verb; two things, a plural verb.

It works in any tense: *se vende*, *se vendió*, *se venderá*.

English needs *was/were* plus a participle. Spanish needs none of that, and there is no "by" phrase. If you want to name who did it, use a normal sentence: *Vale vendió todos los almuerzos*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the *pasiva refleja*, the reflexive passive. You already met the cousin that says *aquí se habla español*.

readAndPick.es: Se firmará el contrato el lunes.
options: The contract was signed on Monday.
The contract will be signed on Monday.
The contract will be signed yesterday.

readAndPick.es: Se abrirá el café en diciembre.
options: The café was opened in December.
The café will be opened in December.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (All the lunches were sold): ___ todos los almuerzos. (Se vendió / Se vendieron)
yourTurn.why: The lunches are plural, so the verb is plural: *vendieron*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (The contract was signed yesterday): ___ el contrato ayer. (Se firmó / Se firmaron)
Type in Spanish: The papers were signed.
yourTurn.why: *Se* plus a plural verb for a plural thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Cards are not accepted.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes before *se*, and the verb is plural because of *tarjetas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it future: Se firmó el contrato.
accept: Se firmará el contrato el lunes.
yourTurn.why: Only the verb changes tense; *se* stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: Se cerró la ventana.
yourTurn.why: The thing is now plural, so the article and the verb are too.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: A waiter is needed.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The verb agrees with the thing sold, and there are many lunches.
That copies the English *were sold*; in everyday Spanish, *se* does the job.

pitfalls.wrong: Se vendieron los almuerzos por Vale.
pitfalls.why: *Se* has no room for "by someone"; when you name who did it, use a normal sentence.
One contract, so the verb stays singular.

personal: Tell us one thing that happens every day where you work or live, using *se*: for example, *Se abre a las ocho*.
